text.content:
Roll 1d8 or choose: the shadow haunting your days, and three questions you may always ask, answered honestly by the GM. From a certain point of view, your suffering is what lets you understand the world.

> Asking carries implications. If the amnesiac asks what memory this moment brings back, the GM cannot answer "none" — the moment does bring one back. In most games that's a table convention. In this world it is not. Attention shapes the Aether; at the margin, the question obliges the answer to exist. Whether it found the truth or made it is a question this game declines to settle.

1d8TormentYour questions
1AMNESIAYou recall very little beyond your name and abilities. Every new memory carries relief… and trepidationWhat happy or painful memory does this moment bring back? · Is there anyone here who remembers me, though I don't remember them? · Are they in control of their own actions?
2BETRAYALWhen someone needed you most, you ran. The blame lies entirely on your shouldersAre they telling the truth? (reads deception, never error — the sincerely wrong ring true) · What is the best way out of here? · Who is the weakest target here?
3DEATHYour hands are stained with blood, and you can never make your peace with itWhat is the best way to hurt them? · What would make them lose control? · What here has killed before?
4WANTYou have been poor in the way that never leaves youWhat is this worth, and to whom? · What does it cost to belong here? · Who here has never gone without?
5FRUSTRATIONAmbition and the fear of failure and judgment have turned you bitter and enviousWhat do they want the most? · Who do they serve? · What do they have that I don't?
6LOSSYou lost the people dearest to you, because you could not protect them. The guilt is a shackleWho here is in the most danger? · What are we overlooking here? · What is most dangerous here?
7REVELATIONYou glimpsed the true complexity of the world, and it shattered your values. You are painfully aware of your own ignoranceWhere can I find that information? (a source — a place, a person, a book — never the answer itself) · What are their true feelings? · What is strange about this place?
8SOLITUDEA lifetime of betrayal and manipulation has convinced you nobody finds you worthy of loyalty. A tool, not a personWhat do they want from me? · How can I get them to do what I want? · What is the best place to hide?

Your Torment is yours — it rides through every mask, and no Guise covers it. Establish what it means for your character when you take it, at the table.
